title: New horizons for the methodology and physiology of training periodization
population: Conceptual review of periodization in high-performance sport; no study population
findings: Lists limitations of traditional periodization: conflicting responses to 'mixed' training of many abilities, excessive fatigue from prolonged multi-targeted training, insufficient stimulation from medium/low-concentration workloads, and inability to provide multi-peak performance over a season.
Block periodization sequences specialised cycles (blocks) with highly concentrated workloads directed to a minimal number of targeted abilities, developed consecutively rather than simultaneously.
The paper sets out general principles, a taxonomy of mesocycle blocks and guidelines for compiling an annual plan.
limitations: Theoretical, narrative review aimed at high-performance sport; the abstract presents no outcome data comparing block with traditional training.
implications: Provides the conceptual basis for an optional block mode (concentrated single-ability blocks) for trained athletes; empirical support is only the low-quality evidence in [molmen-2019-block-periodization-meta-analysis].
No numeric parameters are given; block lengths must be treated as design choices (grade D).

verification.notes: Added by verifier as the core block-periodization source named in scope. Crossref and PubMed match (Sports Med 2010;40(3):189-206, Issurin).
